summary: 76-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation (warfarin stopped after a fall): sudden left leg pain 4 h ago, pale, cold, pulseless below the femoral, numbness beyond the toes and weak toe dorsiflexion — Rutherford IIb.

inputs.hpi: Sudden onset severe pain in the left leg 4 hours ago while watching television. The leg went pale, cold and numb, and she cannot move her toes well. Atrial fibrillation; warfarin stopped 2 months ago after a fall. No previous claudication.

exam.general: Distressed. HR 104 irregularly irregular, BP 148/86, T 36.8°C.
exam.msk: Left leg: pallor with mottling to mid-calf, cold to touch below the knee, pulseless — femoral pulse present, popliteal, dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses absent, no Doppler arterial signal at the ankle. Paraesthesia and sensory loss over the foot beyond the toes; weak toe dorsiflexion (paralysis developing). Calf soft. Right leg pulses present.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute limb ischaemia of left leg (embolic)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute embolic limb ischaemia of the left leg, Rutherford IIb (immediately threatened) — atrial fibrillation off anticoagulation. Needs IV heparin and emergency revascularisation.

mustAlarm.note: A limb-threatening emergency with normal vital signs: only a condition-specific alarm surfaces it.

mustInclude.note: Imaging must not delay revascularisation in IIb.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add an acute limb ischaemia disease and protocol (6 Ps, Rutherford I–III, immediate IV heparin, emergency/urgent revascularisation, CTA only if it will not delay IIb) with ICD I74.2–I74.4, and an ALI red-flag rule in rules.ts (sudden cold pale pulseless limb).

mustExclude.note: A chronic PAD plan in acute ischaemia.

guideline.name: ESVS 2020 clinical practice guidelines — acute limb ischaemia
guideline.section: Clinical diagnosis (pain, pallor, pulselessness, paraesthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia); Rutherford/TASC categories I, IIa, IIb, III; immediate IV heparin unless contraindicated; IIb (immediately threatened) needs emergency revascularisation; IIa urgent; imaging (CTA) must not delay revascularisation in IIb
guideline.citation: Björck M, Earnshaw JJ, Acosta S, et al. European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Acute Limb Ischaemia. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2020;59:173–218.

guideline.name: Rutherford — recommended reporting standards for lower-extremity ischaemia (acute ischaemia categories)
guideline.section: Acute limb ischaemia categories: I viable; IIa marginally threatened (minimal sensory loss, no weakness); IIb immediately threatened (sensory loss beyond toes, rest pain, mild–moderate weakness); III irreversible
guideline.citation: Rutherford RB, Baker JD, Ernst C, et al. Recommended standards for reports dealing with lower extremity ischemia: revised version. J Vasc Surg. 1997;26:517–38.

rationale: Base ALI case: embolic occlusion with all six Ps and motor deficit (Rutherford IIb). Vital signs are near-normal, so the engines must recognise the limb emergency from findings. ESVS 2020: immediate heparin and emergency revascularisation.
